Katanga Mining Ltd Unveils High-Grade Copper Product to Meet Global Demand

Katanga Mining Ltd, a major player in the Democratic Republic of the Congo's (DRC) metals and mining sector, announced the launch of a new high-grade copper cathode product on Tuesday, aiming to strengthen its position in the global supply chain amid robust demand for critical minerals.

The new copper cathode, produced at Katanga’s flagship facility in Lualaba Province, is set to meet international quality standards, with purity levels exceeding 99.99%. Company officials say the product is tailored to meet the needs of global manufacturers, particularly in the electronics and renewable energy sectors, where demand for copper continues to surge.

“We are pleased to introduce our latest copper cathode, which reflects our commitment to innovation and operational excellence,” said Jean-Marc Lavoie, CEO of Katanga Mining Ltd, during the launch event in Kolwezi. “This product enables our customers to access reliable, high-purity copper essential for the technologies of tomorrow.”

Copper is a key component in everything from power grids to electric vehicles, and the DRC is the world’s largest producer of cobalt and among the top producers of copper. Katanga’s new product is expected to bolster the nation’s export portfolio and contribute to local economic growth. The company has invested approximately $45 million in upgrading its refining and processing infrastructure over the past 18 months to support the new line.

Analysts welcomed the launch, noting that the move positions Katanga Mining Ltd to capture a larger share of the fast-growing global copper market. “With copper prices holding firm and supply chains under pressure, Katanga’s high-grade product launch is well-timed,” said Adam Tshiswaka, an independent mining analyst based in Kinshasa. “It demonstrates the ability of Congolese producers to compete at the highest international standards.”

The Congolese Chamber of Mines praised the initiative, highlighting its potential to create new skilled jobs and promote best practices in the sector. “Local beneficiation and value addition are critical for the long-term sustainability of our mining industry,” said Chamber president Marie-Bernadette Ilunga.

Katanga Mining Ltd said it has already secured initial orders from customers in Europe and Asia, and is ramping up marketing efforts to attract further interest. The company reiterated its focus on responsible sourcing and environmental stewardship, emphasizing ongoing efforts to minimize the environmental footprint of its operations.

Shares in Katanga Mining Ltd closed up 2.3% following the announcement.
